title: Chip Earnings Selloff (Qualcomm, Arm, Marvell)
summary: Gotrade News - Qualcomm (QCOM) shares fell 6.46% in after-hours trading on Wednesday, November 4, after fiscal fourth-quarter adjusted EPS of $2.17 landed
body_markdown:
Automotive revenue jumped 89% in the fourth quarter, while handset revenue fell 26%, per the release. For the full fiscal 2026, Qualcomm reported non-GAAP revenue of $43.2 billion and non-GAAP EPS of $10.54.


## Arm Guides Q3 Revenue to $1.54 Billion, Near Consensus


Arm forecast fiscal third-quarter 2027 revenue of $1.54 billion, plus or minus $50 million, and adjusted EPS of 56 cents, plus or minus 4 cents, against consensus of $1.53 billion and 55 cents, according to Investing.com. Seoul Economic Daily noted that some brokerages had projected revenue as high as $1.7 billion.


In the quarter just reported, licensing and other revenue rose 50% to $773 million and royalty revenue reached $670 million, with data center royalties doubling year over year, according to Arm's announcement. Arm said its confidence in "up to $2 billion in Arm AGI CPU revenue over FYE27 and FYE28" has increased, citing purchase orders from multiple customers through calendar 2027 and first commercial deliveries on track for its fiscal fourth quarter.


## Why Did Qualcomm and Arm Stocks Fall?


Seoul Economic Daily tied both declines to a memory shortage, as memory suppliers shifted production toward high-bandwidth memory for AI data centers. "There is no problem with demand; the problem is supply," Amon said, while Arm CEO Rene Haas said, "If we had more supply, we could do more," as quoted by the same outlet.


Per[Seeking Alpha](https://seekingalpha.com/news/4666031-arm-signals-up-to-2b-in-arm-agi-cpu-revenue-across-fiscal-2027minus-2028-as-q3-revenue-seen) 's summary of Arm's earnings call, the risks management flagged included higher memory prices pressuring smartphone sales and supply-chain constraints on AGI CPU deliveries.


## Intel Outlook Sparked the October 30 Chip Selloff


The reactions extend a rough stretch for chip stocks. On October 30, Qualcomm fell 11.7% midday to $163.75 after Intel guided fourth-quarter revenue to $15 billion to $16 billion, below a Wall Street consensus of about $17 billion, as reported by[Investing.com](https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/why-is-qualcomm-stock-tumbling-today-93CH-4988443) . The same report said Arm and[Marvell Technology (MRVL)](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/mrvl/) also sank sharply in the sector-wide selloff.
